verdicts.claim: 1. A closed op tree with two owners per op (fold step + SQL renderer) can express the derived columns analysts reach for, so v1 needs no expression-string or code escape hatch.
verdicts.reason: No escape hatch is the right call, but the op list and its semantics are not yet executable by BOTH owners identically. (a) The stated absence rule ('any absent input makes the result absent') contradicts SQL three-valued logic for and/or (SQL: NULL AND FALSE = FALSE) and contradicts coalesce by definition, so the SQL owner must emit CASE wrappers or the conformance test fails on the first fixture. (b) 'Absent' is defined only as null, but the library's absence is a DECLARED column with a vocabulary (AbsenceDecl, src/def/types.ts:150-157; ColumnFacet.absence, src/data/types.ts:74-80): a row whose report_state is 'unavailable' carries cases=0, not null, so cases/population would compute 0 where the honest answer is absent. (c) Several ops have divergent JS/SQL semantics that must be pinned as a spec: round (Math.round(-2.5) = -2, SQL ROUND = -3), dayOfWeek numbering, week (ISO vs DuckDB week()), string '<' (code units vs collation), lower/upper on non-ASCII. (d) Missing ops analysts reach for first: isAbsent, in-list, case (multi-arm), substring/contains/replace, dateDiff, and any cross-table value (see claim 11). (e) CSV dates are strings (src/data/csv.ts has no date parsing) while TypeTally's 'date' means Date instances (src/data/fold.ts:167), so cast(to date) has no defined output representation.
verdicts.fix: Define absent = null OR the table's AbsenceDecl column not 'present' (evaluated per row, from the declaration); pin every op's semantics in the fixture table with the DuckDB value written beside the fold value (round half-away, isodow, ISO week, byte-order compare); add isAbsent, in, case, substring/contains/replace, dateDiff; make cast(to date) produce an ISO string (the library's date discipline), never a Date; stamp each DerivedColumn with the op-vocabulary version so old declarations still render.

verdicts.claim: 2. materializeColumn plus branch-scoped visibility through the fold is a sufficient landing spot for derived columns, so no new storage path is needed in the memory engine.
verdicts.reason: materializeColumn is one shared physical store mutated in place: row layout writes r[name] = values[i] on every row (src/data/memoryProvider.ts:243-246), with no un-materialize (the session admits it, src/session/session.ts:1186-1189), no collision guard (it silently overwrites a SOURCE column of the same name), and a TALLIED type (store.columnTypes[name] = inferType(values), :250), not the tree's computed type. Branch scoping is metadata-only: effectiveColumnsOf filters columns() (session.ts:1194-1199) but allRows/selectedRows return rowAt's whole row objects (memoryProvider.ts:118-121; session.ts:1163-1170, 1213-1216), so branch B's rows carry branch A's derived values. Two branches declaring the same field with different formulas overwrite each other, formula: null has no path, undo of a column commit leaves the bytes, and a refresh replaces the provider entirely (src/def/buildDashboard.ts:296-304) while materializedByCommit still lists the column. Seek to a past cursor never re-derives.
verdicts.fix: Add a column OVERLAY to the memory provider: derived values stored per (table, field, declaringCommitId) beside the base store, never written into base rows; evaluate/columns take the cursor's visible overlay set (the session passes it from its fold) and project rows explicitly; drop = delete the overlay entry; declaring a field that exists in the base is refused (derive-invalid: 'cases is a source column'); the overlay carries the tree's computed type and derivedAgainst version; a refresh clears overlays and marks them stale rather than losing them silently.

verdicts.claim: 3. Re-deriving declared columns automatically after a refresh is always safe and cheap enough to run in the normal tier, because a declaration can be re-run where an analysis output cannot.
verdicts.reason: Re-runnable, yes; automatic and cheap, not as designed. refresh() lives on the dashboard (buildDashboard.ts:271-315) and no session learns of it — session.ts has no refresh hook; it only reads runtime.sources lazily when stamping a commit (session.ts:516-521) — so 'automatically' has no caller. Derived columns are branch-scoped commits, so 're-derive the declared columns' means every branch's, into one shared store (claim 2's collision). The refresh path already materializes every old row and runs deltaByKey with JSON.stringify per row pair (src/source/delta.ts:33, :39-43) — seconds at 1M before any derivation starts. foldOnce is a synchronous, non-resumable loop (src/data/fold.ts:40-44), so a 1M re-derivation cannot yield to the scheduler's Step contract. 'Safe' also misses a type change: if the refreshed column's TypeTally verdict moved (string→number), a derivation silently computes something else.
verdicts.fix: Refresh writes a journal event and notifies registered sessions (dashboard keeps a listener set); each session marks its cursor's derived columns stale (derivedAgainst ≠ sources[table].version) and re-derives LAZILY on the next read of that column, only the cursor-visible set, under the normal tier; add derive-type-changed as a typed gap when an input's type verdict moved; make the fold resumable (see missing #5) before any 1M re-derivation is promised.

verdicts.claim: 4. One column verb with slots (formula/label/type/role/scale/unit, null = back to the declaration) covers derivation, rename, type fix and drop without a second declaration surface.
verdicts.reason: The shape is consistent with describe/link and the wiring is real work but bounded: DispatchVerb is a closed ten-verb union with a frozen DISPATCH_VERBS list (src/def/types.ts:48-72), keyOf/familyOf are hard-coded prefix arms (src/branches/fold.ts:88-126), rebuildFold routes by prefix (session.ts:672-690), and RESERVED_VIEW_PREFIXES lives in src/def/validate.ts:89-98, not in src/branches/fold.ts as the design says. The slot semantics have three holes: (a) type on a DERIVED column contradicts 'typed by construction' — it must be refused there and allowed only as a declared-type override on source columns (ColumnDecl.type already exists for exactly that, src/encoding/types.ts:192-199); (b) unit has no declaration to fall back to — ColumnDecl has type/role/scale/label only, so null = 'back to the declaration' is undefined for unit; (c) formula: null on a SOURCE field would mean dropping source bytes and must be refused (hide is arrangement). Also role 'absence' is derived from AbsenceDecl and must be refused as a slot value, and facetsOf reads the def only (session.ts:2536) so the fold's overrides need a new consumer path.
verdicts.fix: Slots: formula (derived only; null drops), label, role (never 'absence'), scale, unit (add unit to ColumnDecl first), and type only on source columns as the declared-type override; validator refuses the other combinations with sentences; facetsOf takes the fold's column overrides as a second argument; add column: to RESERVED_VIEW_PREFIXES in validate.ts and extend the prose.test.ts family pin.

verdicts.claim: 5. Sheet arrangement as navigate commits on the layout identity, with widths and scroll excluded, keeps the log free of noise while making a beat's sheet screenshot reproducible.
verdicts.reason: The layout precedent exists and seek does restore it (activeLayouts fold, session.ts:684-689), but doLayoutNote accepts only a plain STRING value (session.ts:2037-2045 refuses non-strings; the fold stores String(rec.value), :687). Sort = {field, dir}, hidden = a set, order = a list, so the sheet must encode them as strings the reader PARSES — against the 'never parsed' rule. Layout commits are inert in keyOf (fold.ts:96), so they never enter planUndo/foldDiff/compare: 'undo my sort' is impossible, and a sort issued from a seeked cursor BRANCHES (R8 branch-on-act) — one branch per sort, the noise the claim says it avoids. Reproducibility: a beat replays sort/hidden/order, but the screenshot's top row depends on the excluded scroll offset, and after a refresh the same offset shows different rows.
verdicts.fix: Either widen doLayoutNote to a JSON-safe validated value (one prop = one fact: sort, hidden, order, frozen), or declare one string grammar per prop and own its parser in src/branches (one place); keep layout inert but let planUndo revert layout props on the same path; record the top visible row KEY (not offset) as a layout prop so a beat reproduces the same first row across versions; suppress branch-on-act for layout notes from a past cursor (treat as a note on the cursor's branch tip) or document the branching.

verdicts.claim: 6. Header stats from one foldOnce over all rows per data version are affordable at 90k and 1M rows without sampling, so the Sampled badge will rarely appear.
verdicts.reason: Step 0 has ALREADY run (bench/step0/REPORT.md, TABLE.md — the design's P0 is partly done and should read it). At 90k the claim holds: a 4-recorder fold is 3.7 ms, columnar+columnTypes over all 13 columns 22.8 ms, so a 30-column profile is tens of ms. At 1M: 4 recorders 28 ms, columnar+types over 6 columns 110 ms, distinct on a unique key (keyedIndex) 56–65 ms per column and a 1M-entry Map in memory; a 30-column profile with extent+groupCount+distinct per column is ~200–600 ms in Node with gc between reps (REPORT assumption #1: browser p95s are optimistic). That crosses the plan's own 200 ms line, so at 1M the profile MUST be on the normal tier — but foldOnce is one synchronous loop (fold.ts:40-44) that cannot be sliced or aborted, so a bounded walk cannot produce a sample at all; the badge would never appear because it cannot. Note the store already computes column types on construction (memoryProvider.ts:88-96) — only stats are extra.
verdicts.fix: Make the profile one RESUMABLE fold (foldSteps(rows, recorders, {from, until}) returning a cursor — the Weave ColumnDataTask.iterate(stopTime) shape) cached per (table, version); cap distinct with a cardinality ceiling that reports '> N distinct' instead of holding a 1M Map; measure the 30-column profile at 1M in the bench (add the row) before promising the badge is rare.

verdicts.claim: 7. The sheet's per-window ViewQuery (limit/offset/sort in rows mode plus count mode) is exactly the rectangle contract every grid needs, so vendor adapters stay thin.
verdicts.reason: The rectangle is the right port, but the engine underneath has neither offset nor sort: EvaluateOptions carries mode/columns/limit only (src/data/types.ts:225-232) and the bench confirms a page at offset 5,000 materializes every match then slices (REPORT 'A virtual SHEET page fetch'). Grid adapters need three more things the design's port omits: (a) a stable row identity per row across windows for selection and copy — rowAt returns bare objects (memoryProvider.ts:118-121) with no key, and an unkeyed table has only positions, which a sort re-numbers; (b) count with every rows answer (EvaluateResult already does this, :246 — keep it); (c) a cap on cells(rect), since Ctrl+C over a 1M-row selection is a whole-table materialization. And in the demo the ui reaches the session over HTTP polling (/api/state, /api/rows — vizfootprint-demo/server/doors.ts:7-8), so a per-scroll window is a network hop there: the port needs an http adapter, not only sessionSheetData. Finally the window MUST pass columns = the cursor's visible set, or claim 2's row leak reaches the grid.
verdicts.fix: Extend EvaluateOptions with offset and sort[{field, dir}], echo the declared key (or a per-version positional id) on each row, answer {rows, count, version, start}; add a cells cap with a typed sheet-unsupported refusal above it; ship two SheetData adapters in P4 (session, http) sharing the block cache; the session adapter always projects to the fold's visible columns.

verdicts.claim: 8. A cached sorted index per (sort, filter, version) epoch makes sort at 1M rows a one-time cost rather than a per-window cost.
verdicts.reason: Sort was never measured (bench-entry.ts has no sort row) and no sort exists in the engine. Keying the cache by FILTER defeats it: every select/filter commit changes activeFilters (the crossfilter law), so each gesture invalidates the index and pays a fresh O(m log m) comparator sort over the matches — on 'select all' that is a 1M-row JS sort per gesture (hundreds of ms), i.e. per-gesture, not one-time. Only the (sort, version) pair is stable across gestures.
verdicts.fix: Cache ONE sorted permutation per (table, sort, version) — built once, ideally over the typed column (Int32Array of indices, typed-array sort for numbers); a window walks the permutation applying the predicate (O(n), the same cost as today's matchingIndices, 24–34 ms at 1M) and offset counts through it; add this walk and the one-time 1M sort to bench/step0 as rows 8 and 9 before P2.

verdicts.claim: 9. DOM virtualization is enough at 90k rows and acceptable at 1M for 30 columns, so canvas is not needed in v1.
verdicts.reason: Nothing in the repo measures the browser side: bench/step0 is Node-only by its own assumption #1, bench/x4 has no grid, and ui/src has no virtualizer today (no react-window/tanstack/virtual anywhere). The field evidence (AG Grid ~40 rendered rows, 500-row cap; regular-table) supports DOM at 90k with FIXED row heights; the real risk at 30 columns is not row count but 1,200 live cells re-rendered per scroll frame with per-cell React elements plus header mini-bars, and the per-window fetch (an HTTP hop in the demo). 'Acceptable at 1M' is a guess until frame time is measured — the plan's own exit rule applies.
verdicts.fix: Fix row height (no measureElement), render cells as plain text nodes with a memoized row, keep header stats out of the scroll path; add a real-Chromium bench in bench/x4 (frame time scrolling 30 columns, time-to-first-paint at 1M) as the P4 gate; keep renderer: dom | canvas a dial with canvas unbuilt.

verdicts.claim: 10. selectedRows' filter as the first view-query customer and the sheet as the second is the lower-risk order and the two counts will match byte for byte.
verdicts.reason: selectedRows is one provider.evaluate(table, clauses, {mode:'rows'}) (session.ts:1213-1216 via allRows :1163-1170) and selectedRowCount is the same clause list in count mode (selectedCount :1219-1224, overview :2519); both funnel through matchingIndices (memoryProvider.ts:127-140) with resolvePredicateSQL as the pinned descriptor (:196-198), so parity is structural, and the refactor has no UI. Caveat only: the oracle exists for the DEFAULT table (selectedCount runs on this.defaultTable) and once the sheet's own header filters land as commits they join activeFilters and change the count they are compared against — the parity test must compare the sheet's count to overview() taken at the same cursor.

verdicts.claim: 11. Aggregate-kind derived columns over a groupBy cover most of what analysts would otherwise need a join for, so leaving joins out of v1 costs little.
verdicts.reason: over: {groupBy} aggregates within ONE table. The design's own first live derivation (P6, 'cases_per_100k') needs population from ANOTHER table keyed by jurisdiction — the demo serves three tables (doors.ts:8) — and the grammar cannot express a value from a second table; the link grammar's FieldMapping coordinates selections, not values. So the very example the document chose is the case the exclusion breaks. The grain argument (fan-out) is right for general joins, but a keyed single-value lookup keeps grain by construction.
verdicts.fix: Add one op, lookup({table, key, field}): a left lookup of ONE value by the target table's declared key (data[t].key), refused at declaration when that key is not unique (keyedIndex.unkeyed > 0) or absent — no fan-out, no grain change, folds in one walk over a keyedIndex built once per version, renders as a scalar subquery / LEFT JOIN ... USING(key) in SQL, and shows in lineage as an INDIRECT JOIN edge. General joins stay out.

verdicts.claim: 12. A refresh as a journal event beside the log (not a commit) is the honest model because refreshed rows are visible to every session regardless of branch.
verdicts.reason: The dashboard-level part is right: refresh swaps the provider for everyone (buildDashboard.ts:296-304) and commits stamp the version at land time (log.ts:160; session.ts:516-521). Three gaps: (a) CommitRecord.data stamps ONLY the default table's version (session.ts:516-521), so a refresh of any other table never shows as dataMoved; (b) the re-derivation report the design puts in the journal is branch-scoped by construction (derived columns are column commits), so 're-derived 3 columns against Y' is a per-session, per-branch fact and cannot live in a dashboard journal without naming which branch; (c) there is no journal module today (src/def/journal.ts does not exist; the 'ref-event journal' precedent is src/branches/refs.ts) and no session hook fires on refresh.
verdicts.fix: Journal = dashboard-level only {table, from, to, retrievedAt, delta, requestedBy}; per-branch staleness derived at read (column fold entry carries derivedAgainst; stale = derivedAgainst ≠ runtime.sources[table].version), never journaled; stamp data for every table a commit's clauses, derivations or link mappings touch, not just the default table.

verdicts.claim: 13. Column lineage written from the tree at declaration in the OpenLineage shape is complete and needs no post-hoc parsing of SQL.
verdicts.reason: No SQL parsing is right — the tree names its {col} inputs. But the tree alone is not complete: INDIRECT inputs are over.groupBy (GROUP_BY), a lookup's key (JOIN, if claim 11's fix lands), and the BASIS — whether an aggregate ran over the full table or the live selection. The library already has this distinction (columns-channel analyses run over the FULL table, session.ts:1231-1237, and why() records an empty input-selection set for them, :2270-2278); the design never states the basis for aggregate kind, so lineage cannot carry the FILTER edge or its absence. A cast that reads a declared type slot also depends on the column DECLARATION commit, which is a commit input, not a column.
verdicts.fix: Lineage record = {inputFields (DIRECT, from {col}), groupBy (INDIRECT GROUP_BY), lookupKeys (INDIRECT JOIN), basis: 'full-table' | commit ids, declarationCommits (type/unit slots read), derivedAgainst version}; rule: derived columns of both kinds run over the full table (a per-selection aggregate is a measure = ViewQuery.reduce, not a column) and the validator says so in words.

verdicts.claim: 14. A generated why-sentence from the tree plus the version stamp answers the questions a non-programmer asks of a column better than a formula or Excel-style arrows.
verdicts.reason: Better than arrows, yes (arrows stop at charts and versions). 'Better than a formula' is a preference claim the reader evidence does not fully back: Wrangler's non-programmers relied on PREVIEWS ('I just look at the picture'), and Data Formulator 2's users caught wrong transforms from the chart/data, not from code or explanations — so a sentence alone is not what catches a wrong column; example rows are. Today's why() returns flat {tier,id,kind} records with 'no prose fields' (src/why/types.ts, CrossTierSlice) and WhyTarget column carries no table (why/types.ts:93-97; key = column name, why/why.ts:80), so the resolver, table qualifier and sentence are all new.
verdicts.fix: Answer = sentence + formula text + N example rows (inputs beside the result, absent rows included) + the absent count + versions; make the sentence a THIRD owner in the op table (fold, sql, words per op) so it cannot drift from what ran; extend WhyTarget column to {kind:'column', table, field} with the column commit as the viz anchor.

missing: Absence in a derived column is defined only as null, while the table's absence is a declared column with a vocabulary (AbsenceDecl, src/def/types.ts:150-157): the design needs one rule for when a measure cell counts as absent, and the SQL owner needs the matching CASE.

Row identity for the grid: rowAt (memoryProvider.ts:118-121) returns bare objects; a table with no declared key has only positions, which a sort re-numbers, so selection, copy and 'annotate row 4021' need a per-version positional id that rides each window.

foldOnce is a synchronous non-resumable loop (src/data/fold.ts:40-44); the scheduler's Step(remainingMs) contract, a sampled profile, and a cancellable re-derivation all need a resumable fold with a cursor, which the design never adds.

Column-name collisions: a derived field equal to a source column, a reserved probe field (RESERVED_PROBE_FIELDS, session.ts:210), or a '~'-bearing name is not checked anywhere in the provider; the validator must own that list.

The demo's ui reaches the session over HTTP (/api/state, /api/rows, vizfootprint-demo/server/doors.ts:7-8), so SheetData needs an http adapter and a versioned block cache, and the window answer size (30 columns × 100 rows of JSON per scroll) belongs in the bench.
CommitRecord.data stamps only the default table (session.ts:516-521); a sheet over a second table has no dataMoved signal.

The distribution mini-bar assumes a 'bins' recorder, but bins.ts (equalWidthBins :109) is post-hoc over a values array and needs the extent first — two passes; either fix edges from the previous version's extent or add a histogram recorder with declared edges.

Step 0 already exists with results (bench/step0/REPORT.md): the design's P0 should extend it (sort, profile over 30 columns, derive recorder, HTTP window) rather than restate it, and its 1M numbers already show whole-table materializations over 50 ms.

Aggregate-kind basis (full table vs live selection) is never declared, yet the session distinguishes them for analyses (session.ts:1231-1237); without the rule, two engines and the lineage will disagree.
Proposal cards evaluate exampleRows — VALUES — on a sample; whats_here today never carries values (session.ts:2521, Q8); the design must say the rows go to the person, not into the agent's context.
Undo/seek of a column commit: the fold drops the key but nothing un-materializes or re-derives (no store path, no seek hook), so time travel over derived columns is unbuilt, not merely unwired.
Copy/TSV rendering of absence states and ISO dates: the absence vocabulary must be written as its words, not blanks, or the copied sheet loses the typed silence the library exists to keep.
